newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Pliva to release H1 results Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Pliva to release H1 results Sept 23.

text.p: Drug maker Pliva, the first Croatian company to get a listing on the London Stock Exchange, said on Monday it would release results for the first half of 1996 on September 23.
"I couldn't say anything more just yet," chief executive Zeljko Covic told journalists. He said the figures would be issued after being reviewed by Pliva's supervisory board.
But it could be inferred from his comments that the company had made a profit for the first six months.
However, Covic declined to speculate on how January-June figures might affect Pliva's share price.
"Shareholders' (profit) expectations are sometimes higher than results, so a stock can go down even though a company makes profit."
Pliva's shares closed last week at 12,000 kuna on the Zagreb Stock Exchange after peaking at 12,100 kuna earlier in the Tuesday-Friday trading week.
Its global depositary receipts (GDRs), issued at 50 to each underlying share, fetched $47.5-$49.9 in London on Monday.
The company posted a net profit of 398.7 million kuna in 1995 on total income of 1.9 billion kuna.
Pliva is the world's fifth largest manufacturer of Vitamin C and sells 40 percent of its output overseas.
It also has one world-class drug, an antibiotic marketed in central and eastern Europe under the name Azithomycin and as Zithoromax under licence by Pfizer Inc in western Europe and the Americas.
